#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproducible, no-model/no-network core regression suite for the leadv2
# plugin. Covers manifest loading, shell syntax, provider routing/runners,
# supervisor isolation, active registry, and Phase-8 completion guards.

set -euo pipefail

# --- root arithmetic (GATE-ROOT-ARITH-01) -------------------------------------
# LOGICAL_DIR: the entry path as written by the caller — symlink NOT resolved.
# It is the only thing that answers "which checkout was this invoked from?".
LOGICAL_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# REPO_ROOT: derived from git, never from ../.. hops. A symlink entry from
# persona-engine resolves to persona-engine's toplevel; a canonical entry (incl.
# any leadv2 worktree lane) resolves to that worktree's toplevel.
REPO_ROOT="$(git -C "$LOGICAL_DIR" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$REPO_ROOT" ] || [ ! -e "$REPO_ROOT/.git" ]; then
  printf -- '[CORE-OFFLINE] FATAL repo_root_unresolvable from=%s resolved=%s\n' \
    "$LOGICAL_DIR" "${REPO_ROOT:-<not-a-git-checkout>}" >&2
  exit 2
fi

# PHYS_TEST_DIR / PLUGIN_ROOT: physical location of THIS file. Plugin-internal
# siblings must resolve into the canonical plugin tree regardless of entry path.
# bash-3.2 safe: manual readlink chain, no `readlink -f` / `realpath`.
_src="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
while [ -L "$_src" ]; do
  _dir="$(cd -P "$(dirname "$_src")" && pwd)"
  _src="$(readlink "$_src")"
  case "$_src" in /*) ;; *) _src="$_dir/$_src" ;; esac
done
PHYS_TEST_DIR="$(cd -P "$(dirname "$_src")" && pwd)"
PLUGIN_ROOT="$(cd -P "$PHYS_TEST_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
TEST_DIR="$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/tests"
unset _src _dir
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

if [ -n "${LEADV2_CORE_OFFLINE_PROBE:-}" ]; then
  printf -- '[CORE-OFFLINE] probe LOGICAL_DIR=%s REPO_ROOT=%s PLUGIN_ROOT=%s TEST_DIR=%s\n' \
    "$LOGICAL_DIR" "$REPO_ROOT" "$PLUGIN_ROOT" "$TEST_DIR"
  exit 0
fi
PASS=0
FAIL=0
MISSING=0

run_check() {
  local name="$1"
  shift
  printf -- '\n[CORE-OFFLINE] %s\n' "$name"
  # A missing suite file must not be indistinguishable from a failing
  # assertion (N-4): preflight `bash <path>` invocations before executing.
  if [[ "$1" == "bash" && "$2" == /* && ! -r "$2" ]]; then
    MISSING=$((MISSING + 1))
    printf -- '[CORE-OFFLINE] MISSING: %s — %s does not exist\n' "$name" "$2" >&2
    return
  fi
  if "$@"; then
    PASS=$((PASS + 1))
  else
    FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
    printf -- '[CORE-OFFLINE] FAILED: %s\n' "$name" >&2
  fi
}

syntax_all() {
  local file
  while IFS= read -r file; do
    bash -n "$file"
  done < <(find "$PLUGIN_ROOT" -type f -name '*.sh' -print | sort)
}

validate_plugin() {
  if ! command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf -- '[CORE-OFFLINE] claude CLI unavailable; manifest validation cannot run\n' >&2
    return 1
  fi
  claude plugin validate "$PLUGIN_ROOT"
}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# N1-EMPTY-LANE-IS-NOT-A-PASS / PREMATURE-NO-WORK-TERMINAL-01 harness.
3	# Besides the original empty/partial/surface cases, proves product-close waits
4	# for provider + process completion, scopes the diff only after worker exit, and
5	# uses dead/timeout rather than no_work when a live worker exceeds the ceiling.
6	set -uo pipefail
7	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
8	PC="${SCRIPT_DIR}/leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh"
9	SURFACE="${SCRIPT_DIR}/leadv2-status-surface.sh"
10	PASS=0; FAIL=0
11	ok()   { printf '[TEST] PASS: %s\n' "$1"; PASS=$((PASS+1)); }
12	bad()  { printf '[TEST] FAIL: %s\n' "$1"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); }
13	assert_eq() { if [[ "$1" == "$2" ]]; then ok "$3"; else bad "$3 (got '$1' want '$2')"; fi; }
14	
15	make_stubs() { # <dir>
16	  local d="$1"
17	  cat > "${d}/resolver.py" <<'PY'
18	print("reviewer=codex"); print("pool=codex"); print("refusal=")
19	PY
20	  cat > "${d}/codex.sh" <<'SH'
21	#!/usr/bin/env bash
22	mkdir -p "$2"; printf 'REVIEW_VERDICT: PASS\nREVIEW_FINDINGS: critical=0 high=0 medium=0 low=0\n' > "$1"
23	SH
24	  chmod +x "${d}/codex.sh"
25	  printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nprintf "%%s\\n" "$*" >> "%s/journal.log"\n' "${d}" > "${d}/journal.sh"
26	  chmod +x "${d}/journal.sh"
27	  printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nprintf "%%s\\n" "$*" >> "%s/ledger.log"\n' "${d}" > "${d}/ledger.sh"
28	  chmod +x "${d}/ledger.sh"
29	}
30	
31	new_repo() {
32	  local root="$1"
33	  mkdir -p "${root}/agent"
34	  ( cd "${root}" && git init -q -b main && git config user.email t@e.com && git config user.name t \
35	    && printf 'seed\n' > agent/seed.py && git add agent/seed.py && git commit -qm seed ) >/dev/null 2>&1
36	}
37	
38	CASE_PIDS=()
39	CASE_REG_DIR=""
40	FAKE_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT=""
41	FAKE_PID=""
42	FAKE_RUNS=""
43	
44	track_pid() { CASE_PIDS+=("$1"); }
45	
46	cleanup_case() { # <sandbox>
47	  local d="$1" pid
48	  for pid in "${CASE_PIDS[@]:-}"; do
49	    [[ -n "${pid}" ]] && kill "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
50	  done
51	  for pid in "${CASE_PIDS[@]:-}"; do
52	    [[ -n "${pid}" ]] && wait "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
53	  done
54	  [[ -n "${CASE_REG_DIR}" ]] && rm -rf "${CASE_REG_DIR}"
55	  rm -rf "${d}"
56	  CASE_PIDS=()
57	  CASE_REG_DIR=""
58	  FAKE_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT=""
59	  FAKE_PID=""
60	  FAKE_RUNS=""
61	}
62	
63	fake_glm_run() { # <sandbox> <repo> <handle> <delay_s> <work_mode:0=empty,1=dirty,2=committed>
64	  local d="$1" root="$2" handle="$3" delay_s="$4" work_mode="$5"
65	  FAKE_RUNS="${d}/glm-runs"
66	  FAKE_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT="${d}/job-registry"
67	  local run_dir="${FAKE_RUNS}/${handle}"
68	  CASE_REG_DIR="${FAKE_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT}/pc-no-work-$$-${RANDOM}"
69	  mkdir -p "${run_dir}" "${CASE_REG_DIR}"
70	  : > "${CASE_REG_DIR}/${handle}"
71	  (
72	    trap 'exit 0' TERM INT
73	    worker_deadline=$(( SECONDS + delay_s ))
74	    while [[ "${SECONDS}" -lt "${worker_deadline}" ]]; do sleep 0.1; done
75	    if [[ "${work_mode}" != 0 ]]; then
76	      printf 'worker diff\n' >> "${root}/agent/seed.py"
77	    fi
78	    if [[ "${work_mode}" == 2 ]]; then
79	      git -C "${root}" add agent/seed.py
80	      git -C "${root}" commit -qm 'stub worker commit'
81	    fi
82	    sed 's/^status: running$/status: complete/' "${run_dir}/meta.yaml" > "${run_dir}/meta.yaml.tmp"
83	    mv "${run_dir}/meta.yaml.tmp" "${run_dir}/meta.yaml"
84	    rm -f "${CASE_REG_DIR}/${handle}"
85	  ) &
86	  FAKE_PID=$!
87	  track_pid "${FAKE_PID}"
88	  printf 'run_id: %s\npid: %s\nstatus: running\n' "${handle}" "${FAKE_PID}" > "${run_dir}/meta.yaml"
89	}
90	
91	# ---- Case 1: empty diff -> no_work / empty_diff, no e2e flag, exit 5 ---------
92	case_empty_no_work() {
93	  local d root
94	  d="$(mktemp -d)"; root="${d}/repo"; mkdir -p "${root}"
95	  new_repo "${root}"; make_stubs "${d}"
96	  CLAUDE_PROJECT_ROOT="${root}" LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="${d}/cache" \
97	    LEADV2_LANE_WORK_ROOT="${root}" \
98	    LEADV2_DISPATCH_LANE_WRITES="agent/seed.py" \
99	    LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN="${d}/journal.sh" LEADV2_DISPATCH_LEDGER_BIN="${d}/ledger.sh" \
100	    LEADV2_GLM_POLICY_RESOLVER="${d}/resolver.py" LEADV2_DISPATCH_CODEX_BIN="${d}/codex.sh" \
101	    bash "${PC}" "${root}" nw1sig001 sonnet "" 1 1 "founder-nw1" >/dev/null 2>&1
102	  local rc=$?
103	  local handoff="${root}/docs/handoff/dispatch-nw1sig001"
104	  assert_eq "${rc}" "5" "empty-diff exits 5"
105	  if [[ -f "${handoff}/review-gate.md" ]] && grep -q '^reason: no_work$' "${handoff}/review-gate.md"; then
106	    ok "review-gate.md reason=no_work"
107	  else bad "review-gate.md reason=no_work (got: $(cat "${handoff}/review-gate.md" 2>/dev/null))"
108	  fi
109	  if [[ ! -f "${handoff}/e2e-gate-passed.flag" ]]; then ok "e2e-gate-passed.flag absent"; else bad "e2e-gate-passed.flag present"; fi
110	  if grep -q 'terminal=no_work cause=empty_diff' "${d}/journal.log" 2>/dev/null; then
111	    ok "ledger decision line terminal=no_work cause=empty_diff"
112	  else bad "ledger decision line missing (got: $(grep review_gate "${d}/journal.log" 2>/dev/null | tail -1))"
113	  fi
114	  rm -rf "${d}"
115	}
116	
117	# ---- Case 2: partial_diff (mixed group) stays refused -----------------------
118	case_partial_stays_refused() {
119	  local d plugin target
120	  d="$(mktemp -d)"; plugin="${d}/plugin-repo"; target="${d}/target-repo"
121	  mkdir -p "${plugin}/scripts" "${target}/.claude/scripts" "${target}/agent"
122	  ( cd "${plugin}" && git init -q -b main && git config user.email t@e.com && git config user.name t \
123	    && printf 'orig\n' > scripts/foo.sh && git add scripts/foo.sh && git commit -qm seed ) >/dev/null 2>&1
124	  printf 'orig\npatched\n' > "${plugin}/scripts/foo.sh"
125	  ( cd "${target}" && git init -q -b main && git config user.email t@e.com && git config user.name t \
126	    && printf 'seed\n' > agent/seed.py && ln -s "${plugin}/scripts/foo.sh" .claude/scripts/foo.sh \
127	    && git add agent/seed.py .claude/scripts/foo.sh && git commit -qm seed ) >/dev/null 2>&1
128	  make_stubs "${d}"
129	  CLAUDE_PROJECT_ROOT="${target}" LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="${d}/cache" \
130	    LEADV2_LANE_WORK_ROOT="${target}" \
131	    LEADV2_DISPATCH_LANE_WRITES="agent/seed.py,.claude/scripts/foo.sh" \
132	    LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN="${d}/journal.sh" LEADV2_DISPATCH_LEDGER_BIN="${d}/ledger.sh" \
133	    LEADV2_GLM_POLICY_RESOLVER="${d}/resolver.py" LEADV2_DISPATCH_CODEX_BIN="${d}/codex.sh" \
134	    bash "${PC}" "${target}" nw2sig002 sonnet "" 0 1 "founder-nw2" >/dev/null 2>&1
135	  local gate="${target}/docs/handoff/dispatch-nw2sig002/review-gate.md"
136	  if [[ -f "${gate}" ]] && grep -q '^reason: partial_diff$' "${gate}"; then
137	    ok "partial_diff stays refused (reason=partial_diff, not no_work)"
138	  else bad "partial_diff should stay refused (got: $(cat "${gate}" 2>/dev/null))"
139	  fi
140	  rm -rf "${d}"
141	}
142	
143	# ---- Case 3 (R1): a no_work terminal row renders RED, never done(...) --------
144	case_surface_no_work_not_done() {
145	  local SB NOW LEDGER DIR
146	  SB="$(mktemp -d)"; DIR="${SB}/state"; LEDGER="${SB}/ledger"; mkdir -p "${DIR}" "${LEDGER}"
147	  NOW=$(( $(date +%s) ))
148	  # 30min old: lands on stale(...) for lack of any live signal, but inside the
149	  # DEAD_TTL window so it is NOT age-dropped before render. task_sig is the 8-char
150	  # sig the surface keys on; the row lives at ${LEDGER_DIR}/${REPO}.jsonl.
151	  local old=$(( NOW - 1800 ))
152	  printf '{"task_sig":"nw3sig00","founder_task_id":"founder-nw3","terminal":"no_work","cause":"empty_diff","created_epoch":%s,"task_id":"founder-nw3"}\n' "${old}" \
153	    > "${LEDGER}/testrepo.jsonl"
154	  : > "${DIR}/active.yaml"
155	  local out
156	  out="$(LEADV2_STATUS_STATE_DIR="${DIR}" \
157	         LEADV2_STATUS_LEDGER_DIR="${LEDGER}" \
158	         LEADV2_STATUS_RUNS_ROOT="${SB}/cache" \
159	         LEADV2_STATUS_REPO="testrepo" \
160	         LEADV2_STATUS_REPO_ROOT="${SB}" \
161	         LEADV2_STATUS_NOW="${NOW}" \
162	         LEADV2_STATUS_TASKS_YAML="${SB}/tasks.yaml" \
163	         bash "${SURFACE}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
164	  if printf '%s' "${out}" | grep -q 'no-work(empty-diff)'; then
165	    ok "surface renders no-work(empty-diff)"
166	  else bad "surface should render no-work(empty-diff) (got: $(printf '%s' "${out}" | grep -i nw3 || echo '<row absent>'))"
167	  fi
168	  if printf '%s' "${out}" | grep -qE 'done\(no_work|done\(terminal\)'; then
169	    bad "R1: no_work row laundered into done(...)"
170	  else ok "R1: no_work row NOT laundered into done(...)"
171	  fi
172	  rm -rf "${SB}"
173	}
174	
175	# ---- Case 4: watcher wakes while worker lives -> no terminal/artifacts ------
176	case_alive_worker_has_no_terminal() {
177	  local d root handle close_pid handoff
178	  d="$(mktemp -d)"; root="${d}/repo"; handle="slow-alive-$$"
179	  mkdir -p "${root}"; new_repo "${root}"; make_stubs "${d}"
180	  fake_glm_run "${d}" "${root}" "${handle}" 30 0
181	  GLM_RUNS_DIR="${FAKE_RUNS}" LEADV2_PC_RUNS_ROOT="${d}" \
182	    LEADV2_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT="${FAKE_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT}" \
183	    LEADV2_PC_WORKER_POLL_S=1 LEADV2_PC_WORKER_MAX_WAIT_S=40 LEADV2_PC_WORKER_LOG_EVERY_S=1 \
184	    LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="${d}/cache" LEADV2_LANE_WORK_ROOT="${root}" \
185	    LEADV2_DISPATCH_LANE_WRITES="agent/seed.py" LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN="${d}/journal.sh" LEADV2_DISPATCH_LEDGER_BIN="${d}/ledger.sh" \
186	    bash "${PC}" "${root}" nw4sig004 glm "${handle}" 0 0 "founder-nw4" >"${d}/close.log" 2>&1 &
187	  close_pid=$!; track_pid "${close_pid}"
188	  for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
189	    grep -q 'status=waiting_worker' "${d}/journal.log" 2>/dev/null && break
190	    sleep 0.1
191	  done
192	  handoff="${root}/docs/handoff/dispatch-nw4sig004"
193	  if [[ ! -f "${handoff}/review-gate.md" ]]; then ok "alive worker has no review-gate.md"; else bad "alive worker wrote review-gate.md"; fi
194	  if [[ ! -f "${handoff}/review.diff" ]]; then ok "alive worker has no early review.diff"; else bad "alive worker wrote review.diff before exit"; fi
195	  if grep -q 'write-terminal' "${d}/ledger.log" 2>/dev/null; then bad "alive worker emitted a terminal row"; else ok "alive worker emits no terminal row"; fi
196	  if grep -q 'product_close task=nw4sig004 status=waiting_worker author=glm handle=' "${d}/journal.log" 2>/dev/null; then
197	    ok "alive worker journals waiting_worker"
198	  else bad "alive worker waiting journal missing"
199	  fi
200	  cleanup_case "${d}"
201	}
202	
203	# ---- Case 5: worker writes, exits -> exit-time diff is non-empty ------------
204	case_diff_measured_after_exit() {
205	  local d root handle close_pid rc handoff
206	  d="$(mktemp -d)"; root="${d}/repo"; handle="slow-diff-$$"
207	  mkdir -p "${root}"; new_repo "${root}"; make_stubs "${d}"
208	  fake_glm_run "${d}" "${root}" "${handle}" 2 1
209	  GLM_RUNS_DIR="${FAKE_RUNS}" LEADV2_PC_RUNS_ROOT="${d}" \
210	    LEADV2_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT="${FAKE_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT}" \
211	    LEADV2_PC_WORKER_POLL_S=1 LEADV2_PC_WORKER_MAX_WAIT_S=15 \
212	    LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="${d}/cache" LEADV2_LANE_WORK_ROOT="${root}" \
213	    LEADV2_DISPATCH_LANE_WRITES="agent/seed.py" LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN="${d}/journal.sh" LEADV2_DISPATCH_LEDGER_BIN="${d}/ledger.sh" \
214	    bash "${PC}" "${root}" nw5sig005 glm "${handle}" 0 0 "founder-nw5" >"${d}/close.log" 2>&1 &
215	  close_pid=$!; track_pid "${close_pid}"
216	  wait "${close_pid}"; rc=$?
217	  handoff="${root}/docs/handoff/dispatch-nw5sig005"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# N1-EMPTY-LANE-IS-NOT-A-PASS / PREMATURE-NO-WORK-TERMINAL-01 harness.
# Besides the original empty/partial/surface cases, proves product-close waits
# for provider + process completion, scopes the diff only after worker exit, and
# uses dead/timeout rather than no_work when a live worker exceeds the ceiling.
set -uo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
PC="${SCRIPT_DIR}/leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh"
SURFACE="${SCRIPT_DIR}/leadv2-status-surface.sh"
PASS=0; FAIL=0
ok()   { printf '[TEST] PASS: %s\n' "$1"; PASS=$((PASS+1)); }
bad()  { printf '[TEST] FAIL: %s\n' "$1"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); }
assert_eq() { if [[ "$1" == "$2" ]]; then ok "$3"; else bad "$3 (got '$1' want '$2')"; fi; }

make_stubs() { # <dir>
  local d="$1"
  cat > "${d}/resolver.py" <<'PY'
print("reviewer=codex"); print("pool=codex"); print("refusal=")
PY
  cat > "${d}/codex.sh" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
mkdir -p "$2"; printf 'REVIEW_VERDICT: PASS\nREVIEW_FINDINGS: critical=0 high=0 medium=0 low=0\n' > "$1"
SH
  chmod +x "${d}/codex.sh"
  printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nprintf "%%s\\n" "$*" >> "%s/journal.log"\n' "${d}" > "${d}/journal.sh"
  chmod +x "${d}/journal.sh"
  printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nprintf "%%s\\n" "$*" >> "%s/ledger.log"\n' "${d}" > "${d}/ledger.sh"
  chmod +x "${d}/ledger.sh"
}

new_repo() {
  local root="$1"
  mkdir -p "${root}/agent"
  ( cd "${root}" && git init -q -b main && git config user.email t@e.com && git config user.name t \
    && printf 'seed\n' > agent/seed.py && git add agent/seed.py && git commit -qm seed ) >/dev/null 2>&1
}

CASE_PIDS=()
CASE_REG_DIR=""
FAKE_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT=""
FAKE_PID=""
FAKE_RUNS=""

track_pid() { CASE_PIDS+=("$1"); }

cleanup_case() { # <sandbox>
  local d="$1" pid
  for pid in "${CASE_PIDS[@]:-}"; do
    [[ -n "${pid}" ]] && kill "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
  done
  for pid in "${CASE_PIDS[@]:-}"; do
    [[ -n "${pid}" ]] && wait "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
  done
  [[ -n "${CASE_REG_DIR}" ]] && rm -rf "${CASE_REG_DIR}"
  rm -rf "${d}"
  CASE_PIDS=()
  CASE_REG_DIR=""
  FAKE_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT=""
  FAKE_PID=""
  FAKE_RUNS=""
}

fake_glm_run() { # <sandbox> <repo> <handle> <delay_s> <work_mode:0=empty,1=dirty,2=committed>
  local d="$1" root="$2" handle="$3" delay_s="$4" work_mode="$5"
  FAKE_RUNS="${d}/glm-runs"
  FAKE_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT="${d}/job-registry"
  local run_dir="${FAKE_RUNS}/${handle}"
  CASE_REG_DIR="${FAKE_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT}/pc-no-work-$$-${RANDOM}"
  mkdir -p "${run_dir}" "${CASE_REG_DIR}"
  : > "${CASE_REG_DIR}/${handle}"
  (
    trap 'exit 0' TERM INT
    worker_deadline=$(( SECONDS + delay_s ))
    while [[ "${SECONDS}" -lt "${worker_deadline}" ]]; do sleep 0.1; done
    if [[ "${work_mode}" != 0 ]]; then
      printf 'worker diff\n' >> "${root}/agent/seed.py"
    fi
    if [[ "${work_mode}" == 2 ]]; then
      git -C "${root}" add agent/seed.py
      git -C "${root}" commit -qm 'stub worker commit'
    fi
    sed 's/^status: running$/status: complete/' "${run_dir}/meta.yaml" > "${run_dir}/meta.yaml.tmp"
    mv "${run_dir}/meta.yaml.tmp" "${run_dir}/meta.yaml"
    rm -f "${CASE_REG_DIR}/${handle}"
  ) &
  FAKE_PID=$!
  track_pid "${FAKE_PID}"
  printf 'run_id: %s\npid: %s\nstatus: running\n' "${handle}" "${FAKE_PID}" > "${run_dir}/meta.yaml"
}

# ---- Case 1: empty diff -> no_work / empty_diff, no e2e flag, exit 5 ---------
case_empty_no_work() {
  local d root
  d="$(mktemp -d)"; root="${d}/repo"; mkdir -p "${root}"
  new_repo "${root}"; make_stubs "${d}"
  CLAUDE_PROJECT_ROOT="${root}" LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="${d}/cache" \
    LEADV2_LANE_WORK_ROOT="${root}" \
    LEADV2_DISPATCH_LANE_WRITES="agent/seed.py" \
    LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN="${d}/journal.sh" LEADV2_DISPATCH_LEDGER_BIN="${d}/ledger.sh" \
    LEADV2_GLM_POLICY_RESOLVER="${d}/resolver.py" LEADV2_DISPATCH_CODEX_BIN="${d}/codex.sh" \
    bash "${PC}" "${root}" nw1sig001 sonnet "" 1 1 "founder-nw1" >/dev/null 2>&1
  local rc=$?
  local handoff="${root}/docs/handoff/dispatch-nw1sig001"
  assert_eq "${rc}" "5" "empty-diff exits 5"
  if [[ -f "${handoff}/review-gate.md" ]] && grep -q '^reason: no_work$' "${handoff}/review-gate.md"; then
    ok "review-gate.md reason=no_work"
  else bad "review-gate.md reason=no_work (got: $(cat "${handoff}/review-gate.md" 2>/dev/null))"
  fi
  if [[ ! -f "${handoff}/e2e-gate-passed.flag" ]]; then ok "e2e-gate-passed.flag absent"; else bad "e2e-gate-passed.flag present"; fi
  if grep -q 'terminal=no_work cause=empty_diff' "${d}/journal.log" 2>/dev/null; then
    ok "ledger decision line terminal=no_work cause=empty_diff"
  else bad "ledger decision line missing (got: $(grep review_gate "${d}/journal.log" 2>/dev/null | tail -1))"
  fi
  rm -rf "${d}"
}

return 0
  fi

  local poll_s="${LEADV2_PC_WORKER_POLL_S:-10}"
  local max_wait_s="${LEADV2_PC_WORKER_MAX_WAIT_S:-4200}"
  local log_every_s="${LEADV2_PC_WORKER_LOG_EVERY_S:-300}"
  local lease_refresh_s="${LEADV2_PC_LEASE_REFRESH_EVERY_S:-300}"
  [[ "${poll_s}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || poll_s=10
  [[ "${max_wait_s}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || max_wait_s=4200
  [[ "${log_every_s}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || log_every_s=300
  [[ "${lease_refresh_s}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || lease_refresh_s=300

  local started now last_log=0 last_lease_refresh=0 remaining sleep_s
  local lease_extend_s=$(( max_wait_s + poll_s + 20 ))
  started="$(date +%s)"
  while true; do
    now="$(date +%s)"
    _PC_WORKER_WAITED_S=$(( now - started ))
    if [[ "${_PC_WORKER_WAITED_S}" -ge "${max_wait_s}" ]]; then
      return 1
    fi
    # Bound the potentially-slow Codex probe by the watcher's remaining wall
    # clock budget. Without this, a final 20s probe plus a full poll sleep could
    # overshoot a tightened ceiling by roughly 30 seconds.
    remaining=$(( max_wait_s - _PC_WORKER_WAITED_S ))
    _PC_WORKER_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S=20
    [[ "${remaining}" -lt "${_PC_WORKER_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S}" ]] && _PC_WORKER_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S="${remaining}"
    if ! pc_worker_alive; then
      now="$(date +%s)"
      _PC_WORKER_WAITED_S=$(( now - started ))
      return 0
    fi
    now="$(date +%s)"
    _PC_WORKER_WAITED_S=$(( now - started ))
    if [[ "${_PC_WORKER_WAITED_S}" -ge "${max_wait_s}" ]]; then
      return 1
    fi
    if [[ "${last_lease_refresh}" -eq 0 || $(( now - last_lease_refresh )) -ge "${lease_refresh_s}" ]]; then
      _pc_refresh_founder_lease "${lease_extend_s}"
      last_lease_refresh="${now}"
    fi
    if [[ "${last_log}" -eq 0 || $(( now - last_log )) -ge "${log_every_s}" ]]; then
      emit decision "product_close task=${TASK} status=waiting_worker author=${AUTHOR} handle=${HANDLE} waited=${_PC_WORKER_WAITED_S}s"
      # QUESTION-DELIVERY-OWNERSHIP-01: push-deliver unanswered questions
      # belonging to THIS task so the lead session's watchers/journal see them
      # without any founder input. Runs at the same log-interval — no new
      # daemon, piggybacks on the existing 10s poll.
      _pc_emit_pending_questions
      last_log="${now}"
    fi
    remaining=$(( max_wait_s - _PC_WORKER_WAITED_S ))
    sleep_s="${poll_s}"
    [[ "${remaining}" -lt "${sleep_s}" ]] && sleep_s="${remaining}"
    sleep "${sleep_s}"
  done

emit() { # type text
  if [[ -f "${JOURNAL_BIN}" ]]; then bash "${JOURNAL_BIN}" append "dispatch-${TASK}" "$1" "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
  printf '[leadv2-dispatch-product-close] %s\n' "$2" >&2
}

# Phase stamps into active.yaml (SUPERVISOR-AUDIT-01 addendum, founder 2026-07-30) — see
# leadv2-dispatch-code.sh's matching block for the full rationale (fix-fanout made the
# funnel the row's lifecycle owner; nothing ever advanced `phase` past "spawning"). This
# script owns the e2e/review half of the same funnel run, so it stamps those two
# transitions with the same cheap update_phase PATCH; dispatch-code.sh stamps prepass/build.
# Keyed by FOUNDER_TASK_ID (fanout's active.yaml row id), never TASK (the internal sig8) --
# guarded against empty/unset so leadv2_active_update_phase's "${1:?...}" can never abort
# this script under `set -u` when no founder id was threaded through (e.g. a bare re-run).
_ACTIVE_REGISTRY_SH="${SCRIPT_DIR}/leadv2-active-registry.sh"
[[ -f "${_ACTIVE_REGISTRY_SH}" ]] && source "${_ACTIVE_REGISTRY_SH}"
# SILENT-DEATH-01 (SUPERVISOR-AUDIT-01, 2026-07-30): leadv2-active-registry.sh's own
# `set -euo pipefail` (line 26) leaks into this shell via `source` and silently overrides
# this script's own `set -uo pipefail` (line 7, deliberately no -e) -- see
# leadv2-dispatch-code.sh's matching block for the full mechanism. Restore immediately.
set +e
_stamp_active_phase() { # <task_id> <phase>
  [[ -n "${1:-}" ]] || return 0
  declare -F leadv2_active_update_phase >/dev/null || return 0
  LEADV2_PROJECT_ROOT="${ROOT}" leadv2_active_update_phase "$1" "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# N1-EMPTY-LANE-IS-NOT-A-PASS / PREMATURE-NO-WORK-TERMINAL-01 harness.
# Besides the original empty/partial/surface cases, proves product-close waits
# for provider + process completion, scopes the diff only after worker exit, and
# uses dead/timeout rather than no_work when a live worker exceeds the ceiling.
set -uo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
PC="${SCRIPT_DIR}/leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh"
SURFACE="${SCRIPT_DIR}/leadv2-status-surface.sh"
PASS=0; FAIL=0
ok()   { printf '[TEST] PASS: %s\n' "$1"; PASS=$((PASS+1)); }
bad()  { printf '[TEST] FAIL: %s\n' "$1"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); }
assert_eq() { if [[ "$1" == "$2" ]]; then ok "$3"; else bad "$3 (got '$1' want '$2')"; fi; }

make_stubs() { # <dir>
  local d="$1"
  cat > "${d}/resolver.py" <<'PY'
print("reviewer=codex"); print("pool=codex"); print("refusal=")
PY
  cat > "${d}/codex.sh" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
mkdir -p "$2"; printf 'REVIEW_VERDICT: PASS\nREVIEW_FINDINGS: critical=0 high=0 medium=0 low=0\n' > "$1"
SH
  chmod +x "${d}/codex.sh"
  printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nprintf "%%s\\n" "$*" >> "%s/journal.log"\n' "${d}" > "${d}/journal.sh"
  chmod +x "${d}/journal.sh"
  printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nprintf "%%s\\n" "$*" >> "%s/ledger.log"\n' "${d}" > "${d}/ledger.sh"
  chmod +x "${d}/ledger.sh"
}

new_repo() {
  local root="$1"
  mkdir -p "${root}/agent"
  ( cd "${root}" && git init -q -b main && git config user.email t@e.com && git config user.name t \
    && printf 'seed\n' > agent/seed.py && git add agent/seed.py && git commit -qm seed ) >/dev/null 2>&1
}

CASE_PIDS=()
CASE_REG_DIR=""
FAKE_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT=""
FAKE_PID=""
FAKE_RUNS=""

track_pid() { CASE_PIDS+=("$1"); }

cleanup_case() { # <sandbox>
  local d="$1" pid
  for pid in "${CASE_PIDS[@]:-}"; do
    [[ -n "${pid}" ]] && kill "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
  done
  for pid in "${CASE_PIDS[@]:-}"; do
    [[ -n "${pid}" ]] && wait "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
  done
  [[ -n "${CASE_REG_DIR}" ]] && rm -rf "${CASE_REG_DIR}"
  rm -rf "${d}"
  CASE_PIDS=()
  CASE_REG_DIR=""
  FAKE_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT=""
  FAKE_PID=""
  FAKE_RUNS=""
}

fake_glm_run() { # <sandbox> <repo> <handle> <delay_s> <work_mode:0=empty,1=dirty,2=committed>
  local d="$1" root="$2" handle="$3" delay_s="$4" work_mode="$5"
  FAKE_RUNS="${d}/glm-runs"
  FAKE_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT="${d}/job-registry"
  local run_dir="${FAKE_RUNS}/${handle}"
  CASE_REG_DIR="${FAKE_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT}/pc-no-work-$$-${RANDOM}"
  mkdir -p "${run_dir}" "${CASE_REG_DIR}"
  : > "${CASE_REG_DIR}/${handle}"
  (
    trap 'exit 0' TERM INT
    worker_deadline=$(( SECONDS + delay_s ))
    while [[ "${SECONDS}" -lt "${worker_deadline}" ]]; do sleep 0.1; done
    if [[ "${work_mode}" != 0 ]]; then
      printf 'worker diff\n' >> "${root}/agent/seed.py"
    fi
    if [[ "${work_mode}" == 2 ]]; then
      git -C "${root}" add agent/seed.py
      git -C "${root}" commit -qm 'stub worker commit'
    fi
    sed 's/^status: running$/status: complete/' "${run_dir}/meta.yaml" > "${run_dir}/meta.yaml.tmp"
    mv "${run_dir}/meta.yaml.tmp" "${run_dir}/meta.yaml"
    rm -f "${CASE_REG_DIR}/${handle}"
  ) &
  FAKE_PID=$!
  track_pid "${FAKE_PID}"
  printf 'run_id: %s\npid: %s\nstatus: running\n' "${handle}" "${FAKE_PID}" > "${run_dir}/meta.yaml"
}

# ---- Case 1: empty diff -> no_work / empty_diff, no e2e flag, exit 5 ---------
case_empty_no_work() {
  local d root
  d="$(mktemp -d)"; root="${d}/repo"; mkdir -p "${root}"
  new_repo "${root}"; make_stubs "${d}"
  CLAUDE_PROJECT_ROOT="${root}" LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="${d}/cache" \
    LEADV2_LANE_WORK_ROOT="${root}" \
    LEADV2_DISPATCH_LANE_WRITES="agent/seed.py" \
    LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN="${d}/journal.sh" LEADV2_DISPATCH_LEDGER_BIN="${d}/ledger.sh" \
    LEADV2_GLM_POLICY_RESOLVER="${d}/resolver.py" LEADV2_DISPATCH_CODEX_BIN="${d}/codex.sh" \
    bash "${PC}" "${root}" nw1sig001 sonnet "" 1 1 "founder-nw1" >/dev/null 2>&1
  local rc=$?
  local handoff="${root}/docs/handoff/dispatch-nw1sig001"
  assert_eq "${rc}" "5" "empty-diff exits 5"
  if [[ -f "${handoff}/review-gate.md" ]] && grep -q '^reason: no_work$' "${handoff}/review-gate.md"; then
    ok "review-gate.md reason=no_work"
  else bad "review-gate.md reason=no_work (got: $(cat "${handoff}/review-gate.md" 2>/dev/null))"
  fi
  if [[ ! -f "${handoff}/e2e-gate-passed.flag" ]]; then ok "e2e-gate-passed.flag absent"; else bad "e2e-gate-passed.flag present"; fi
  if grep -q 'terminal=no_work cause=empty_diff' "${d}/journal.log" 2>/dev/null; then
    ok "ledger decision line terminal=no_work cause=empty_diff"
  else bad "ledger decision line missing (got: $(grep review_gate "${d}/journal.log" 2>/dev/null | tail -1))"
  fi
  rm -rf "${d}"
}

# ---- Case 2: partial_diff (mixed group) stays refused -----------------------
case_partial_stays_refused() {
  local d plugin target
  d="$(mktemp -d)"; plugin="${d}/plugin-repo"; target="${d}/target-repo"
  mkdir -p "${plugin}/scripts" "${target}/.claude/scripts" "${target}/agent"
  ( cd "${plugin}" && git init -q -b main && git config user.email t@e.com && git config user.name t \
    && printf 'orig\n' > scripts/foo.sh && git add scripts/foo.sh && git commit -qm seed ) >/dev/null 2>&1
  printf 'orig\npatched\n' > "${plugin}/scripts/foo.sh"
  ( cd "${target}" && git init -q -b main && git config user.email t@e.com && git config user.name t \
    && printf 'seed\n' > agent/seed.py && ln -s "${plugin}/scripts/foo.sh" .claude/scripts/foo.sh \
    && git add agent/seed.py .claude/scripts/foo.sh && git commit -qm seed ) >/dev/null 2>&1
  make_stubs "${d}"
  CLAUDE_PROJECT_ROOT="${target}" LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="${d}/cache" \
    LEADV2_LANE_WORK_ROOT="${target}" \
    LEADV2_DISPATCH_LANE_WRITES="agent/seed.py,.claude/scripts/foo.sh" \
    LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN="${d}/journal.sh" LEADV2_DISPATCH_LEDGER_BIN="${d}/ledger.sh" \
    LEADV2_GLM_POLICY_RESOLVER="${d}/resolver.py" LEADV2_DISPATCH_CODEX_BIN="${d}/codex.sh" \
    bash "${PC}" "${target}" nw2sig002 sonnet "" 0 1 "founder-nw2" >/dev/null 2>&1
  local gate="${target}/docs/handoff/dispatch-nw2sig002/review-gate.md"
  if [[ -f "${gate}" ]] && grep -q '^reason: partial_diff$' "${gate}"; then
    ok "partial_diff stays refused (reason=partial_diff, not no_work)"
  else bad "partial_diff should stay refused (got: $(cat "${gate}" 2>/dev/null))"
  fi
  rm -rf "${d}"
}

# ---- Case 3 (R1): a no_work terminal row renders RED, never done(...) --------
case_surface_no_work_not_done() {
  local SB NOW LEDGER DIR
  SB="$(mktemp -d)"; DIR="${SB}/state"; LEDGER="${SB}/ledger"; mkdir -p "${DIR}" "${LEDGER}"
  NOW=$(( $(date +%s) ))
  # 30min old: lands on stale(...) for lack of any live signal, but inside the
  # DEAD_TTL window so it is NOT age-dropped before render. task_sig is the 8-char
  # sig the surface keys on; the row lives at ${LEDGER_DIR}/${REPO}.jsonl.
  local old=$(( NOW - 1800 ))
  printf '{"task_sig":"nw3sig00","founder_task_id":"founder-nw3","terminal":"no_work","cause":"empty_diff","created_epoch":%s,"task_id":"founder-nw3"}\n' "${old}" \
    > "${LEDGER}/testrepo.jsonl"
  : > "${DIR}/active.yaml"
  local out
  out="$(LEADV2_STATUS_STATE_DIR="${DIR}" \
         LEADV2_STATUS_LEDGER_DIR="${LEDGER}" \
         LEADV2_STATUS_RUNS_ROOT="${SB}/cache" \
         LEADV2_STATUS_REPO="testrepo" \
         LEADV2_STATUS_REPO_ROOT="${SB}" \
         LEADV2_STATUS_NOW="${NOW}" \
         LEADV2_STATUS_TASKS_YAML="${SB}/tasks.yaml" \
         bash "${SURFACE}" 2>/dev/null || true)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# N1-EMPTY-LANE-IS-NOT-A-PASS / PREMATURE-NO-WORK-TERMINAL-01 harness.
# Besides the original empty/partial/surface cases, proves product-close waits
# for provider + process completion, scopes the diff only after worker exit, and
# uses dead/timeout rather than no_work when a live worker exceeds the ceiling.
set -uo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
PC="${SCRIPT_DIR}/leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh"
SURFACE="${SCRIPT_DIR}/leadv2-status-surface.sh"
PASS=0; FAIL=0
ok()   { printf '[TEST] PASS: %s\n' "$1"; PASS=$((PASS+1)); }
bad()  { printf '[TEST] FAIL: %s\n' "$1"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); }
assert_eq() { if [[ "$1" == "$2" ]]; then ok "$3"; else bad "$3 (got '$1' want '$2')"; fi; }

make_stubs() { # <dir>
  local d="$1"
  cat > "${d}/resolver.py" <<'PY'
print("reviewer=codex"); print("pool=codex"); print("refusal=")
PY
  cat > "${d}/codex.sh" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
mkdir -p "$2"; printf 'REVIEW_VERDICT: PASS\nREVIEW_FINDINGS: critical=0 high=0 medium=0 low=0\n' > "$1"
SH
  chmod +x "${d}/codex.sh"
  printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nprintf "%%s\\n" "$*" >> "%s/journal.log"\n' "${d}" > "${d}/journal.sh"
  chmod +x "${d}/journal.sh"
  printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nprintf "%%s\\n" "$*" >> "%s/ledger.log"\n' "${d}" > "${d}/ledger.sh"
  chmod +x "${d}/ledger.sh"
}

new_repo() {
  local root="$1"
  mkdir -p "${root}/agent"
  ( cd "${root}" && git init -q -b main && git config user.email t@e.com && git config user.name t \
    && printf 'seed\n' > agent/seed.py && git add agent/seed.py && git commit -qm seed ) >/dev/null 2>&1
}

CASE_PIDS=()
CASE_REG_DIR=""
FAKE_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT=""
FAKE_PID=""
FAKE_RUNS=""

track_pid() { CASE_PIDS+=("$1"); }

cleanup_case() { # <sandbox>
  local d="$1" pid
  for pid in "${CASE_PIDS[@]:-}"; do
    [[ -n "${pid}" ]] && kill "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
  done
  for pid in "${CASE_PIDS[@]:-}"; do
    [[ -n "${pid}" ]] && wait "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
  done
  [[ -n "${CASE_REG_DIR}" ]] && rm -rf "${CASE_REG_DIR}"
  rm -rf "${d}"
  CASE_PIDS=()
  CASE_REG_DIR=""
  FAKE_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT=""
  FAKE_PID=""
  FAKE_RUNS=""
}

fake_glm_run() { # <sandbox> <repo> <handle> <delay_s> <work_mode:0=empty,1=dirty,2=committed>
  local d="$1" root="$2" handle="$3" delay_s="$4" work_mode="$5"
  FAKE_RUNS="${d}/glm-runs"
  FAKE_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT="${d}/job-registry"
  local run_dir="${FAKE_RUNS}/${handle}"
  CASE_REG_DIR="${FAKE_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT}/pc-no-work-$$-${RANDOM}"
  mkdir -p "${run_dir}" "${CASE_REG_DIR}"
  : > "${CASE_REG_DIR}/${handle}"
  (
    trap 'exit 0' TERM INT
    worker_deadline=$(( SECONDS + delay_s ))
    while [[ "${SECONDS}" -lt "${worker_deadline}" ]]; do sleep 0.1; done
    if [[ "${work_mode}" != 0 ]]; then
      printf 'worker diff\n' >> "${root}/agent/seed.py"
    fi
    if [[ "${work_mode}" == 2 ]]; then
      git -C "${root}" add agent/seed.py
      git -C "${root}" commit -qm 'stub worker commit'
    fi
    sed 's/^status: running$/status: complete/' "${run_dir}/meta.yaml" > "${run_dir}/meta.yaml.tmp"
    mv "${run_dir}/meta.yaml.tmp" "${run_dir}/meta.yaml"
    rm -f "${CASE_REG_DIR}/${handle}"
  ) &
  FAKE_PID=$!
  track_pid "${FAKE_PID}"
  printf 'run_id: %s\npid: %s\nstatus: running\n' "${handle}" "${FAKE_PID}" > "${run_dir}/meta.yaml"
}

# ---- Case 1: empty diff -> no_work / empty_diff, no e2e flag, exit 5 ---------
case_empty_no_work() {
  local d root
  d="$(mktemp -d)"; root="${d}/repo"; mkdir -p "${root}"
  new_repo "${root}"; make_stubs "${d}"
  CLAUDE_PROJECT_ROOT="${root}" LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="${d}/cache" \
    LEADV2_LANE_WORK_ROOT="${root}" \
    LEADV2_DISPATCH_LANE_WRITES="agent/seed.py" \
    LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN="${d}/journal.sh" LEADV2_DISPATCH_LEDGER_BIN="${d}/ledger.sh" \
    LEADV2_GLM_POLICY_RESOLVER="${d}/resolver.py" LEADV2_DISPATCH_CODEX_BIN="${d}/codex.sh" \
    bash "${PC}" "${root}" nw1sig001 sonnet "" 1 1 "founder-nw1" >/dev/null 2>&1
  local rc=$?
  local handoff="${root}/docs/handoff/dispatch-nw1sig001"
  assert_eq "${rc}" "5" "empty-diff exits 5"
  if [[ -f "${handoff}/review-gate.md" ]] && grep -q '^reason: no_work$' "${handoff}/review-gate.md"; then
    ok "review-gate.md reason=no_work"
  else bad "review-gate.md reason=no_work (got: $(cat "${handoff}/review-gate.md" 2>/dev/null))"
  fi
  if [[ ! -f "${handoff}/e2e-gate-passed.flag" ]]; then ok "e2e-gate-passed.flag absent"; else bad "e2e-gate-passed.flag present"; fi
  if grep -q 'terminal=no_work cause=empty_diff' "${d}/journal.log" 2>/dev/null; then
    ok "ledger decision line terminal=no_work cause=empty_diff"
  else bad "ledger decision line missing (got: $(grep review_gate "${d}/journal.log" 2>/dev/null | tail -1))"
  fi
  rm -rf "${d}"
}

# ---- Case 2: partial_diff (mixed group) stays refused -----------------------
case_partial_stays_refused() {
  local d plugin target
  d="$(mktemp -d)"; plugin="${d}/plugin-repo"; target="${d}/target-repo"
  mkdir -p "${plugin}/scripts" "${target}/.claude/scripts" "${target}/agent"
  ( cd "${plugin}" && git init -q -b main && git config user.email t@e.com && git config user.name t \
    && printf 'orig\n' > scripts/foo.sh && git add scripts/foo.sh && git commit -qm seed ) >/dev/null 2>&1
  printf 'orig\npatched\n' > "${plugin}/scripts/foo.sh"
  ( cd "${target}" && git init -q -b main && git config user.email t@e.com && git config user.name t \
    && printf 'seed\n' > agent/seed.py && ln -s "${plugin}/scripts/foo.sh" .claude/scripts/foo.sh \
    && git add agent/seed.py .claude/scripts/foo.sh && git commit -qm seed ) >/dev/null 2>&1
  make_stubs "${d}"
  CLAUDE_PROJECT_ROOT="${target}" LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="${d}/cache" \
    LEADV2_LANE_WORK_ROOT="${target}" \
    LEADV2_DISPATCH_LANE_WRITES="agent/seed.py,.claude/scripts/foo.sh" \
    LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN="${d}/journal.sh" LEADV2_DISPATCH_LEDGER_BIN="${d}/ledger.sh" \
    LEADV2_GLM_POLICY_RESOLVER="${d}/resolver.py" LEADV2_DISPATCH_CODEX_BIN="${d}/codex.sh" \
    bash "${PC}" "${target}" nw2sig002 sonnet "" 0 1 "founder-nw2" >/dev/null 2>&1
  local gate="${target}/docs/handoff/dispatch-nw2sig002/review-gate.md"
  if [[ -f "${gate}" ]] && grep -q '^reason: partial_diff$' "${gate}"; then
    ok "partial_diff stays refused (reason=partial_diff, not no_work)"
  else bad "partial_diff should stay refused (got: $(cat "${gate}" 2>/dev/null))"
  fi
  rm -rf "${d}"
}

# ---- Case 3 (R1): a no_work terminal row renders RED, never done(...) --------
case_surface_no_work_not_done() {
  local SB NOW LEDGER DIR
  SB="$(mktemp -d)"; DIR="${SB}/state"; LEDGER="${SB}/ledger"; mkdir -p "${DIR}" "${LEDGER}"
  NOW=$(( $(date +%s) ))
  # 30min old: lands on stale(...) for lack of any live signal, but inside the
  # DEAD_TTL window so it is NOT age-dropped before render. task_sig is the 8-char
  # sig the surface keys on; the row lives at ${LEDGER_DIR}/${REPO}.jsonl.
  local old=$(( NOW - 1800 ))
  printf '{"task_sig":"nw3sig00","founder_task_id":"founder-nw3","terminal":"no_work","cause":"empty_diff","created_epoch":%s,"task_id":"founder-nw3"}\n' "${old}" \
    > "${LEDGER}/testrepo.jsonl"
  : > "${DIR}/active.yaml"
  local out
  out="$(LEADV2_STATUS_STATE_DIR="${DIR}" \
         LEADV2_STATUS_LEDGER_DIR="${LEDGER}" \
         LEADV2_STATUS_RUNS_ROOT="${SB}/cache" \
         LEADV2_STATUS_REPO="testrepo" \
         LEADV2_STATUS_REPO_ROOT="${SB}" \
         LEADV2_STATUS_NOW="${NOW}" \
         LEADV2_STATUS_TASKS_YAML="${SB}/tasks.yaml" \
         bash "${SURFACE}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if printf '%s' "${out}" | grep -q 'no-work(empty-diff)'; then
    ok "surface renders no-work(empty-diff)"
  else bad "surface should render no-work(empty-diff) (got: $(printf '%s' "${out}" | grep -i nw3 || echo '<row absent>'))"
  fi
  if printf '%s' "${out}" | grep -qE 'done\(no_work|done\(terminal\)'; then
    bad "R1: no_work row laundered into done(...)"
  else ok "R1: no_work row NOT laundered into done(...)"
  fi
  rm -rf "${SB}"
}

# ---- Case 4: watcher wakes while worker lives -> no terminal/artifacts ------
case_alive_worker_has_no_terminal() {
  local d root handle close_pid handoff
  d="$(mktemp -d)"; root="${d}/repo"; handle="slow-alive-$$"

  if grep -q 'write-terminal' "${d}/ledger.log" 2>/dev/null; then bad "alive worker emitted a terminal row"; else ok "alive worker emits no terminal row"; fi

    rc=$?; elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - started ))
    gate="${root}/docs/handoff/dispatch-nwrv000${idx}/review-gate.md"
    assert_eq "${rc}" "5" "${status} reaches ordinary empty-diff terminal"
    # CORE-OFFLINE-TIMING-FLAKE-01: "ignores the stale handle" used to be proven by
    # elapsed<2s (max_wait_s), which also measures bash-fork + script-source overhead
    # that has nothing to do with the poll loop -- under real CPU contention on this
    # box (concurrent leadv2 lanes + AV scanning, load avg regularly 8-12 on 10 cores)
    # that overhead alone can exceed 2s and the assertion goes red for a reason the
    # code never caused. The loop only ever journals "status=waiting_worker" for a
    # handle AFTER pc_worker_alive() reports it still alive (see product-close's wait
    # loop) -- so absence of that line for this task is the same "resolved on the
    # very first check, never entered the wait loop" proof, with zero wall-clock
    # dependency. A real regression that starts polling the stale handle still fails

# ---- Case 3 (R1): a no_work terminal row renders RED, never done(...) --------
case_surface_no_work_not_done() {

  # 30min old: lands on stale(...) for lack of any live signal, but inside the

  # CORE-OFFLINE-TIMING-FLAKE-01: the registry-clear timer must clear meaningfully
  # later than one noisy poll iteration can take, or a single slow iteration (python3
  # + bash subprocess spawn under real CPU contention) races past it and the loop
  # finishes after 1-2 calls instead of the 3+ this case exists to prove. 6s (with

n=$(cat "${LEADV2_TEST_LIVENESS_COUNT}")

if [[ "${n}" -lt 2 ]]; then

# ---- Case 10: GLM/Kimi revival finalizes the original stale registry handle -
case_revived_status_is_terminal_for_handle() {
  local status idx d root handle runs reg rc started elapsed gate
  idx=0
  for status in revived revive_blocked_by_gate; do
    idx=$((idx + 1))
    d="$(mktemp -d)"; root="${d}/repo"; handle="revived-${idx}-$$"
    mkdir -p "${root}"; new_repo "${root}"; make_stubs "${d}"
    runs="${d}/glm-runs"; reg="${d}/job-registry/revive-case"
    mkdir -p "${runs}/${handle}" "${reg}"
    printf 'run_id: %s\nstatus: %s\nrevived_to: replacement-run\n' "${handle}" "${status}" > "${runs}/${handle}/meta.yaml"
    : > "${reg}/${handle}"
    started="$(date +%s)"
    GLM_RUNS_DIR="${runs}" LEADV2_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT="${d}/job-registry" \
      LEADV2_PC_WORKER_POLL_S=1 LEADV2_PC_WORKER_MAX_WAIT_S=2 \
      LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="${d}/cache" LEADV2_LANE_WORK_ROOT="${root}" \
      LEADV2_DISPATCH_LANE_WRITES="agent/seed.py" LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN="${d}/journal.sh" LEADV2_DISPATCH_LEDGER_BIN="${d}/ledger.sh" \
      bash "${PC}" "${root}" "nwrv000${idx}" glm "${handle}" 0 0 "founder-revive-${idx}" >"${d}/close.log" 2>&1
    rc=$?; elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - started ))
    gate="${root}/docs/handoff/dispatch-nwrv000${idx}/review-gate.md"
    assert_eq "${rc}" "5" "${status} reaches ordinary empty-diff terminal"
    # CORE-OFFLINE-TIMING-FLAKE-01: "ignores the stale handle" used to be proven by
    # elapsed<2s (max_wait_s), which also measures bash-fork + script-source overhead
    # that has nothing to do with the poll loop -- under real CPU contention on this
    # box (concurrent leadv2 lanes + AV scanning, load avg regularly 8-12 on 10 cores)
    # that overhead alone can exceed 2s and the assertion goes red for a reason the
    # code never caused. The loop only ever journals "status=waiting_worker" for a
    # handle AFTER pc_worker_alive() reports it still alive (see product-close's wait
    # loop) -- so absence of that line for this task is the same "resolved on the
    # very first check, never entered the wait loop" proof, with zero wall-clock
    # dependency. A real regression that starts polling the stale handle still fails
    # this the same way it always did: the line would appear.
    if ! grep -q "task=nwrv000${idx} status=waiting_worker" "${d}/journal.log" 2>/dev/null \
      && grep -q '^reason: no_work$' "${gate}" 2>/dev/null; then
      ok "${status} ignores stale original registry handle"
    else bad "${status} waited to timeout instead of finalizing original handle"
    fi
    if grep -q ' dead timeout' "${d}/ledger.log" 2>/dev/null; then bad "${status} wrote permanent dead/timeout"; else ok "${status} never writes dead/timeout"; fi
    cleanup_case "${d}"
  done
}

# run-core-offline.sh red on clean main — ROUND 2 — developer full report

## Repro (before any change)

Standalone `test-no-work-terminal.sh` on this worktree, run alone, passed 43/43 on
every attempt (multiple runs). It only fails inside `run-core-offline.sh`'s full
sequential run, and even there it does not fail every time — it is a flake, not a
deterministic red.

## Hypothesis 1 (codex quota lockout silently changes the assertion's code path) — REFUTED

Evidence:
- `case_codex_probe_waits` (case 8) and `case_revived_status_is_terminal_for_handle`
  (case 10) both fully mock the codex/glm provider surface: `LEADV2_LANE_LIVENESS_BIN`
  points at a test-local stub script, `LEADV2_JOB_REGISTRY_ROOT` and
  `LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR` are sandboxed under a fresh `mktemp -d`. Neither case
  reads any real quota-lockout file under `~/.claude/cache` — I traced every call site
  (`_pc_codex_provider_state`, `_pc_maybe_quota_advance`) and confirmed the lockout
  directory used by the glm/kimi quota-advance path (only reachable from case 8's glm
  sibling suites, not the codex branch these two cases exercise) resolves under the
  sandboxed `LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR`, never the real one.
- Real codex quota has been locked out since 2026-08-06 (per mission) and still is —
  yet the suite passed 43/43 standalone, repeatedly, on this exact box, during this
  session. If the lockout were short-circuiting the code path the assertions depend
  on, the failure would be deterministic, not intermittent. It is intermittent.

**Conclusion: quota lockout is not the cause. Do not accept this hypothesis for future
rounds without re-deriving — it was checked directly, not assumed.**

## Actual root cause: wall-clock assertions too tight for this box's real CPU contention

This is a genuinely shared, loaded dev box, not evidence-free assumption:
- `uptime` showed load averages of 8-12 (on a 10-core Mac) at baseline during this
  session, before I added any load of my own.
- `ps aux` showed **two other live `leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh` processes**
  running concurrently for the `persona-engine` project while I worked — i.e. real,
  independent lanes contending for the same CPU at the same time as any suite run.
- Sophos antivirus (`com.sophos.endpoint.scanextension`, `SophosCryptoGuard`,
  `SophosEventMonitor`) consistently consumes 150-300%+ combined CPU on this machine
  in the background, unrelated to anything leadv2 does.
- Direct measurement: five back-to-back `python3 + bash` subprocess spawns (the exact
  shape `_pc_codex_provider_state` performs once per poll) took 0.12s-0.48s each under
  this baseline load — call overhead that is not fixed, and that eats directly into
  the loop's fixed `LEADV2_PC_WORKER_POLL_S` cadence.

Two assertions were tight enough that this overhead alone could flip them red without
any code regression:

1. **Case 10 (`revived`/`revive_blocked_by_gate`)**: asserted `elapsed<2s` against a
   `LEADV2_PC_WORKER_MAX_WAIT_S=2` ceiling. `elapsed` is measured from *before* `bash
   "${PC}" ...` forks, so it also counts process-fork + script-source overhead that has
   nothing to do with the poll loop being tested. Under load that alone can exceed 2s.
2. **Case 8 (codex probe polled through done)**: needed >=3 liveness-probe calls to
   land inside a fixed 10s ceiling, synchronized against an independent background
   `(sleep 3; rm ...)` clearing the fake job-registry entry. If any single poll
   iteration's subprocess spawn (python3+bash) is slow enough to push the *next* check
   past the 3s clear point, the loop finishes after only 1-2 calls — exactly the
   "codex liveness probe called only 2 times" failure from the mission brief.

## Fix applied (plugins/leadv2/scripts/tests/test-no-work-terminal.sh only)

**Case 10**: replaced the `elapsed<2s` wall-clock proxy with a structural,
zero-wall-clock-dependent check. Reading `pc_worker_alive`'s wait loop in
`leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh` (lines ~891-930): it only ever journals
`status=waiting_worker` for a handle *after* `pc_worker_alive()` reports the handle
still alive, and before sleeping for the next poll. So "resolved on the very first
check, never entered the wait loop" is exactly equivalent to "no
`status=waiting_worker` line for this task ever appears in journal.log" — true
regardless of how slow the surrounding process fork/script-source overhead is. I
verified this is still discriminating: I temporarily broke
`leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh`'s revived/revive_blocked_by_gate short-circuit
(`[[ "${status}" == revived || ... ]] && return 1`) with a hardcoded `false`, reran
the case standalone, and confirmed the new assertion goes red (`status=waiting_worker`
line appears) exactly as the old one did. Restored the file after (verified `git diff`
clean) and reran green.

**Case 8**: widened the two purely load-shaped windows rather than the invariant
itself — `LEADV2_PC_WORKER_MAX_WAIT_S` 10s->30s and the background registry-clear
timer 3s->6s (elapsed threshold correspondingly 3s->4s). This does not change what the
case proves (still: liveness probe polled more than once, past a registry entry that
is still live) — it only gives the fixed poll cadence enough headroom that one slow
iteration under contention can't race past the clear point prematurely. The
`calls>=3` and now `elapsed>=4` assertions are unchanged in spirit and still fail if
a regression under-polls or short-circuits early.

Neither change touches the code under test (`leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh`) or
weakens what either case is capable of catching — both are pure test-file edits, and
both were verified red-then-green against a deliberately broken lifecycle (case 10
directly; case 8's invariant — poll multiple times before finishing — was not
independently broken-and-restored due to time, but its logic is untouched, only the
timing margins around it changed).

## Wall-clock: before / after

- **Before** (this box, this session): a full `run-core-offline.sh` run with `timeout
  590` did not finish (`rc=124`) inside the mission's cited 600s ceiling — user+sys CPU
  time was only ~161s of that 590s wall-clock (27% average utilization), meaning ~73%
  of the wall time was the process sitting blocked on CPU scheduling, not doing work.
  That run passed test-no-work-terminal.sh's 43 assertions cleanly (no flake that
  time) but got stuck deep into a later, unrelated, legitimately slow suite
  (`test-routing-enforcement-p1.sh` — dispatch refusal fallback chain — which alone
  took multiple minutes for its ~15 real-dispatch-simulation subtests) and never
  reached a verdict inside the budget I gave it.
- **After** (my fix, standalone): `test-no-work-terminal.sh` alone: 43/43 passed,
  ~34s wall-clock (was ~35s before under similar concurrent load, ~4s faster on a
  quiet box) — the widened case-8 window adds a few seconds in the worst case, not
  materially different in the common case.
- I did **not** find or fix a hang in `test-no-work-terminal.sh` itself — it never
  hung in any of my runs, timed or untimed, standalone or from
  `run-core-offline.sh`. The multi-minute-plus overrun that ate the mission's 600s
  budget lives in later suites (`test-routing-enforcement-p1.sh` visibly, likely also
  `test-supervise-v2.sh`'s hardcoded `sleep 15`), amplified by this box's persistent
  background contention (concurrent leadv2 lanes for other projects + Sophos AV). Both
  of those suites are outside this mission's scope (mission: "Two other suites are red
  on untouched main for unrelated reasons and are not yours" — these aren't red, but
  they are the actual source of the >10-minute wall-clock, and I did not touch them).

## What I deliberately left alone

- `test-routing-enforcement-p1.sh` and `test-supervise-v2.sh` — both structurally slow
  independent of the flake this mission targets; changing their internals is a
  separate, larger decision (mission's own hard limits forbid raising the gate
  timeout to hide symptoms, and rewriting unrelated suites' real-dispatch-simulation
  timing is exactly that kind of larger, separate call).
- `leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh` — untouched. The two fixed assertions were test
  fixture problems (wall-clock margins too tight for this box), not a code defect in
  the script under test.
- No SKIP-count / codex-availability gating was added, per the "explicitly out of
  scope" list — not needed, since the quota-lockout hypothesis was refuted.

## Platform

macOS (Darwin 25.5.0), this dev box (`/Users/kostiantyn.vlasenko/Projects/leadv2/.claude/worktrees/be4c2e83`),
bash 3.2-compatible syntax throughout (`bash -n` and `shellcheck -x` both clean on the
changed file). Not run on the Linux VPS — I don't have access to it from this
subsession; the mission's own hard limits note this box's behavior may differ from
Linux and that Linux is preferred where available.

DELIVERABLE_COMPLETE

The >10-minute overrun traces to other legitimately slow suites (`test-routing-enforcement-p1.sh` visibly took minutes even when passing) amplified by this box's persistent background load — out of scope for this mission and left untouched.
